claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a dual-phase FCC/B2 microstructure.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy is ductile.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 at approximately 600°C induces a brittle state.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 at approximately 750°C produces or restores a ductile state.
Aging near 600°C forms near-stoichiometric Ni3Al-type L12 ordered domains within the FCC matrix.
Near-stoichiometric L12 ordering maximizes the antiphase-boundary energy in the FCC matrix.
Jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries are preserved in the brittle, approximately 600°C-aged condition.
High antiphase-boundary energy inhibits dislocation cross-slip and forces planar slip.
Planar slip bands interacting with jagged B2/FCC boundaries produce stress concentrations at boundary serrations.
Stress concentration at serrated phase boundaries causes intergranular or transgranular fracture.
Higher-temperature aging reduces the L12 long-range order parameter and lowers antiphase-boundary energy.
Reduced L12 ordering increases the local intrinsic stacking-fault energy.
Aging near 750°C forms ductile transition zones along B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Ductile transition zones facilitate cross-slip and blunt stress concentrations, thereby restoring ductility.
Elongation is lowest when L12 ordering is maximal and phase boundaries are jagged, and recovers when ordering decreases and boundaries become smoother or chemically modified.
The brittle state requires an L12 long-range order parameter above a critical value together with a highly serrated B2/FCC interface.
Ductility is restored when the order parameter falls below the critical value or the interface becomes smooth or chemically graded.
Lower-temperature phase decomposition, including sigma-phase formation, occurs in a related CrMnFeCoNi alloy system.
Antiphase-boundary energy can be inferred from superlattice-dislocation pair spacing in TEM for the proposed alloy and conditions.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations modify magnetic-entropy contributions to stacking-fault energy in CoCrFeMnNi.

contradictions.description: The brittle window is described as extending through 750°C and ductility is said to return above 750°C, but other fields classify the 750°C-aged condition itself as ductile and predict recovery at 750°C.
